UBUNTU 26.04 · PATCHED OPEN DRIVER 615.71.09 · TURING + AMPERE · EXPERIMENTAL

GPU-to-GPU P2P across two GPU generations

An RTX 2060 (Turing) and an RTX 3060 (Ampere), which CUDA normally refuses to pair. Two routes, every byte checked.
BUILT ON
aikitoria libcuda patch for mixed generationsnoon-at-cgn P2P driver and BAR1 resizetinygrad original GeForce P2P patchNVIDIA open kernel modules
ADDED HERE
The USB-C step: the 2060's own USB-C functions blocked its memory window. Removed, it grows from 256 MB to 8 GB, enough for the driver to allow P2P.
Without P2P: through the computer's main memory With P2P: straight to the other GPU
ROUTE 1 · CUDA PEER ACCESS
Patched driver + a patched copy of libcuda
CUDA treats the pair like two cards of one generation, so NCCL, PyTorch and vLLM use it unchanged (NCCL all-reduce +43%). 4 bytes changed in a copy; runs as a normal user.

ROUTE 2 · I/O MEMORY
Patched driver + the other card's memory window
Vulkan maps one card's VRAM through its BAR1; CUDA on the other card registers it as I/O memory and writes straight in. Only programs written for it; root and one opt-in fork key.
